relationships.subject: PACAP
relationships.evidence_quote: PACAP-38 injection into the mouse dura mater produced a sustained increase in periorbital allodynia lasting up to 24 hours, which was dependent on the MrgprB2 receptor (27).

relationships.subject: CGRP receptor antagonist olcegepant
relationships.evidence_quote: This sensitization is not reversed by the CGRP receptor antagonist olcegepant (95), consistent with PACAP and CGRP mediating allodynia by distinct and independent mechanisms.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP primarily signals through two receptor complexes, CLR/RAMP1 (canonical) and CTR/RAMP1 (AMY1) (38).

relationships.subject: PACAP
relationships.evidence_quote: PACAP induces mechanical cephalic allodynia in mice of both sexes following subcutaneous injection (61,95)

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP induces mechanical cephalic allodynia in mice regardless of the sex with intraperitoneal (98), subcutaneous (95) and periorbital injections (96).

relationships.subject: PACAP
relationships.evidence_quote: Jansen-Olesen et al. (15) reported a concentration-dependent release of CGRP by PACAP-38 in the trigeminal nucleus caudalis but not in the trigeminal ganglia.

key_findings: PACAP and CGRP induce similar migraine-like behaviors in mice via largely independent pathways; PACAP effects persist in RAMP1 knockout mice and with CGRP antibody.
CGRP is more abundant in trigeminal neurons whereas PACAP is prominent in sphenopalatine ganglia; PACAP engages Epac/MAPK and Gq-calcium more than CGRP.
